intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (PVRL1; 600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 nonsense mutation has been associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (orofacial cleft 7; OFC7), which is included here.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (PVRL1).
checks.evidence_quote: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous loss-of-function mutations of the poliovirus receptor-like 1 (PVRL1) gene encoding nectin-1.
checks.explanation: Stated directly; NECTIN1 is the approved symbol for PVRL1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no chromosomal location. The location is standard gene annotation for the gene the paper names, so under the stated rule it counts as supported.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 nonsense mutation has been associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (orofacial cleft 7; OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports that heterozygosity for the PVRL1 (NECTIN1) nonsense mutation W185X is associated with sporadic non-syndromic CL/P. The 'OFC7' label is OMIM nomenclature that the paper does not use.

paragraphs.text: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder. Suzuki et al. (1998) listed its features as unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate. Some patients also have mental retardation (Zlotogora et al., 1987; Rodini and Richieri-Costa, 1990; Yoshida et al., 2015).

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4) is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: The paper calls ED4 autosomal recessive. ED4 is the earlier designation for the disorder the draft names cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) listed the features of cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome as unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families that were probably related to each other. The families came from a relatively isolated, inbred population on Margarita Island (Nueva Esparta State) in northeastern Venezuela. All affected individuals had ectodermal dysplasia along with other anomalies. Females were affected as severely as males, and expressivity varied. The authors concluded that the clinical picture did not fit any known ectodermal dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome. He was the first child of a consanguineous marriage. He had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia. He also had a distinctive facial appearance with cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers, and mild mental retardation. On scanning electron microscopy, his hair showed pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi.

paragraphs.text: In a 7-year-old Japanese boy with CLPED1 born to consanguineous parents, Yoshida et al. (2015) analyzed exon 2 of the PVRL1 gene and found a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C-T (R134X). Both parents were heterozygous for the mutation. The authors noted that all 4 PVRL1 mutations reported in this syndrome so far, including this one, produce truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1. These domains are needed to start the cell-cell adhesion process.

paragraphs.text: Homozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation trp185-to-ter (W185X) causes the autosomal recessive syndrome CLPED1 on Margarita Island. Sozen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for W185X and sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela.

checks.claim: Homozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation trp185-to-ter (W185X) causes the autosomal recessive syndrome CLPED1 on Margarita Island.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly. 'trp185-to-ter' is the same variant as W185X written in different notation.

checks.claim: Sozen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 W185X mutation and sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Yoshida et al. (2015) studied a 7-year-old Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome, the child of a consanguineous marriage. He had a novel homozygous c.400C-T transition in exon 2 of the PVRL1 gene, resulting in an arg134-to-ter (R134X) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous for the mutation. The predicted truncated protein lacks the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1, which are needed to start cell-cell adhesion.

checks.claim: Yoshida et al. (2015) studied a 7-year-old Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome who was the child of a consanguineous marriage.
checks.evidence_quote: A 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The Japanese boy studied by Yoshida et al. (2015) had a novel homozygous c.400C-T transition in exon 2 of the PVRL1 gene, resulting in an arg134-to-ter (R134X) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of exon 2 of PVRL1 revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*).
checks.explanation: Stated directly; C>T is a transition, and the notations are equivalent.

checks.claim: Both parents of the Japanese boy studied by Yoshida et al. (2015) were heterozygous for the PVRL1 R134X mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: His parents were heterozygous for the mutant alleles.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The predicted truncated protein from the PVRL1 R134X mutation lacks the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1.
checks.evidence_quote: including this study, resulted in truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1 are needed to start cell-cell adhesion.
checks.evidence_quote: lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1, which is necessary to initiate the cell-cell adhesion process.
checks.explanation: Stated directly; the abstract's singular 'is' could refer to the intracellular domain alone, but it is read here as both domains.
